Cipolla, Carlo M.

Clocks and culture, 1300-1700 / Carlo M. Cipolla ; [introduction by Anthony Grafton].

How did a time-keeping device affect the growth of crafts guilds and the scientific research that led to the Industrial Revolution in Europe? Why were Chinese Mandarins enchanted by the intricate workings of clocks but uninterested in their time-keeping function? While European life quickly became regulated by the ticking of town clocks, Asia retained its seasonal cycles of time and initially resisted the idea of living life by the clock. Clocks and Culture is a brief history of the changes wrought by and on Europe and Asia over four hundred years due to technological advances in time-keeping and the rise of a clock-centered culture. - Publisher.

# Clocks and Culture, 1300-1700

Image: Front CoverCarlo M. CipollaNorton, 1977 - History - 191 pages How did a time-keeping device affect the growth of crafts guilds and the scientific research that led to the Industrial Revolution? Clocks and Culture is a brief history of the changes wrought by and on Europe over four hundred years due to technological advances in timekeeping and the rise of a time-aware culture. In his introduction, Anthony Grafton, Henry Putnam University Professor of History at Princeton University, puts this classic book in perspective.

Les horloges, l'Occident et la Chine1 C'est un peu comme une méditation sur les rapports entre la civilisation et la technologie que se présente le petit ouvrage de Carlo M. Cipolla ; il pose le problème très actuel du danger de la technique sans la science et un humanisme correspondant et envisage successivement les réponses données à l'intrusion de la technique dans la civilisation par l'Europe moderne et par la Chine mandarinale. De toutes les merveilles nées de l'habileté et du génie inventif de l'Occident, il n'en est peut-être aucune qui ait eu plus d'influence sur le comportement, la manière de penser — jusqu'à l'image de Dieu — - et l'attitude devant la vie que celle qui permet de mesurer le temps. 1.
